title: Ctrl+Alt+Timeline
blurb: Your feed, your playlist, your paycheck, and the plot twists behind all three.

cards.say: Netflix [turned down a 15 million dollar offer from Amazon in 1998], [tried to sell itself to Blockbuster for 50 million dollars in 2000], [mailed out VHS tapes until it switched to DVDs in 1999], and [mailed out its very last rental DVD in 2023].
cards.real: Netflix never rented VHS. Tapes were too bulky to mail cheaply, so it shipped DVDs from the start.

cards.say: Vine [shut down for good in January 2019], [was bought by Twitter for 30 million dollars in 2012], [dropped its famous six-second limit in 2016], and [had its stars move into one apartment complex on Vine Street].
cards.real: Twitter announced the shutdown in October 2016, and Vine closed on January 18, 2017.

cards.say: Rickrolling [got Rick Astley voted Best Act Ever at the 2008 MTV Europe Music Awards], [put Rick Astley on a float in the 2008 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade], [was pulled on followers by the White House's Twitter account in 2011], and [began in 2007 as a fake link to a Halo 3 trailer].
cards.real: The first rickroll, in May 2007, was a link dressed up as a trailer for Grand Theft Auto IV.

cards.say: Bitcoin [was first described in a paper posted on Halloween 2008], [had its very first block mined on New Year's Day 2009], [hid a London newspaper headline inside its very first block], and [was used to buy two pizzas for 10,000 bitcoins in 2010].
cards.real: The first block was mined on January 3, 2009, with a headline from that day's Times of London tucked inside.

cards.say: The Ice Bucket Challenge [got buckets dumped on both LeBron James and Bill Gates], [sent 77 million dollars of its haul to research], [helped pay for research that found a new ALS gene in 2016], and [raised more than 115 million dollars in a single weekend].
cards.real: The 115 million dollars came in over about eight weeks in the summer of 2014, not in one weekend.

cards.say: Twitter [got the hashtag from its own founders in 2007], [bought its first bird logo from a stock image site for under 20 dollars], [had its very first tweet sold as an NFT for about 2.9 million dollars], and [didn't make hashtags clickable until 2009].
cards.real: Blogger Chris Messina proposed the hashtag in an August 2007 tweet, and Twitter didn't adopt it right away.

cards.say: Instagram [had 13 employees when Facebook bought it for a billion dollars], [didn't come out for Android phones until 2012], [started out under the name Picaboo], and [openly admitted copying its Stories feature from Snapchat].
cards.real: Picaboo was Snapchat's original name in 2011. Instagram launched as Instagram, on the iPhone, in October 2010.

cards.say: Myspace [was the most visited website in the US in 2006], [was co-founded by Justin Timberlake in 2003], [sold for 35 million dollars, six years after selling for 580 million], and [lost more than 50 million uploaded songs in a server move].
cards.real: Tom Anderson and Chris DeWolfe created Myspace in 2003. Justin Timberlake came in as a part-owner in 2011.

cards.say: Slack [was bought by Microsoft for 27.7 billion dollars], [began as a chat tool inside a company making an online game], [is named for Searchable Log of All Conversation and Knowledge], and [signed up 8,000 customers in its first day].
cards.real: Salesforce bought Slack for about 27.7 billion dollars. The deal was announced in December 2020 and closed in July 2021.

cards.say: The Return of the King [won every one of the 11 Oscars it was up for], [won Best Picture without a single acting nomination], [was the second movie ever to make a billion dollars], and [was the first sequel ever to win Best Picture].
cards.real: The Godfather Part II was the first sequel to win Best Picture, for 1974. The Return of the King was the second, 29 years later.

cards.say: Stranger Things [was first pitched under the title Montauk], [named Chief Hopper after a character in Jaws], [was turned down by more than a dozen networks before Netflix], and [had about 1,000 kids audition with lines from Stand by Me].
cards.real: Chief Hopper is named after a commando in the 1987 movie Predator.

cards.say: Blockbuster [had about 9,000 stores at its peak], [didn't offer online rentals until 2004], [was down to one last store, in Alaska, by 2019], and [ended up with a last store that opened in 1992 as Pacific Video].
cards.real: In 2019 the last Blockbuster on Earth was the one in Bend, Oregon.
